activities.name: petSpongeCompare

config.prompt: Drag across what an oil field actually is:

before.label: the picture most people carry
before.text: Petroleum pools in underground lakes and caverns — a well 'runs dry' the way a glass empties.

after.label: the reality
after.text: Ordinary sandstone or limestone whose microscopic pore spaces happen to be full of hydrocarbons, buried kilometres down — salty water below, often gas above.

config.why: No pool to pump dry, only pore space to drain cubic metre by cubic metre from kilometres of rock — which is why production declines gradually and a well can flow for decades.

activities.anchor: basins where the water was starved of oxygen, decay stalled
activities.caption: sequence the making of a source rock
activities.name: petSourceOrder

config.prompt: From sunshine to source rock, in order:
items: Plankton and algae photosynthesise in ancient seas and lakes
The remains sink where the deep water lets nothing finish breaking them down
Successive mud layers bury the organic goo, slowly becoming dark shale
The organic-rich shale is the source rock — burial is the cooking
config.why: Petroleum is fossil sunshine: the whole chain is a race between burial and decomposition, won only in oxygen-poor basins.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the dinosaur theory
activities.name: petDinoSpot

config.prompt: One line of this origin story is wrong — click it:
lines: Petroleum is organic — that much the popular picture gets right.
The organic matter in oil is overwhelmingly marine plankton and algae.
Populations of large animals could easily supply the quantities involved.
Most oil predates the dinosaurs by hundreds of millions of years.
One-line answer: oil is mostly compressed ancient plankton, cooked by burial heat.
config.correction: No population of large animals could ever supply the volume — the organic matter is overwhelmingly marine plankton and algae.
config.why: A grain of truth (petroleum is organic) wrapped around an arithmetic impossibility.

activities.anchor: a journey that can cover tens or even hundreds of kilometres
activities.caption: pair each migration concept with its mechanism
activities.name: petTrapMatch

config.prompt: Catching a wandering fluid — pair the terms:

pairs.right: oil at 0.8–0.9 g/cm³ rides above brine at 1.0–1.1 — salad oil above vinegar
built by deformation: the anticline's crest, faults smeared with clay
built by the rocks themselves: pinch-outs, reefs ringed by tight mudrock
the impermeable cap — shale, or best of all rock salt

config.why: And in every trap the fluids settle by density — gas on top, oil beneath, water at the bottom — a three-layer column every reservoir engineer pictures blind.

config.prompt: Porosity or permeability — file each fact:

items.label: the fraction of the rock's volume that is void
a good sandstone runs 15–30 per cent
compaction squeezes pores shut; cement destroys them
how fast water would move through the sponge
depends steeply on the largest pores and their connectedness

config.why: Related but not the same: pumice holds plenty and gives none; a fractured granite holds little and gives it fast.

config.text: Gas condensates exist as %%0%% underground but drop valuable liquids as pressure falls; dry gas is nearly pure %%1%%; and within the oil itself the four hydrocarbon families mix — alkanes, %%2%%, aromatics and asphaltics.
config.hint: The phase up top, the simplest molecule, and the ring-shaped family.

items: Primary — ride the reservoir's own energy: dissolved gas expanding, a gas cap pushing down, an aquifer pushing up (typically 5–20 per cent)
Secondary — inject water to maintain pressure and sweep oil toward producers (toward 30–50 per cent)
Enhanced — attack the physics: steam thins heavy oil, CO2 swells it, chemical floods lower interfacial tension
The standing challenge — even then, roughly half the oil typically stays underground
config.why: Each rung manipulates a term of the same physics — pressure, sweep, viscosity and tension — that Darcy's law listed.

config.prompt: 7758 × 2,000 acres × 50 ft × 0.20 porosity × 0.75 ÷ 1.2 — roughly how many stock-tank barrels of oil initially in place?
config.why: About 97 million — which is why the answer ships as P90/P50/P10 cases: porosity from logs calibrated to cores, saturation from resistivity, volume factor from the lab.
config.context: geology arrives as probabilities, not answers
